query: Who is considered the true founder of the Delhi Sultanate and why?

politely refused to give him shelter, and by doing so, saved India from the threat of a Mongol

territories in India into a strong, well-defined, compact state. Iltutmish completed the Qutb Minar and also built his own tomb in Delhi.

Iltutmish completed the Qutb Minar and also built his own tomb in Delhi. Learned scholars from
various parts of Asia found refuge in his court. He was the first to mint gold and silver coins, and
organized the revenue departments of the Sultanate. The Sultanate was divided into several
provinces called iqtas. Each iqta was administered by an officer or noble called the iqtadar. The Caliph of Baghdad recognized Iltutmish as the sovereign of India.

A temple at

ground_truth: Iltutmish is regarded as the true founder of the Delhi Sultanate because he transformed the loosely-knit territories in India into a strong, well-defined, compact state, and consolidated and stabilized the kingdom after dealing with external and internal threats.

query: What happened to Razia Sultan and why did her nobles oppose her?
ideal_context:

Both men and women should be given equal opportunities to learn and grow. There should be no

7. Razia Sultan
Iltutmish nominated his daughter Razia as his successor. His nobles did not like the idea of being
ruled by a woman. So Razia had to prove her qualities of a great monarch. She dressed like a man,
transacted business in the open durbar, and rode horses and led the armies into battle. The welfare
of her subjects was her primary duty. Later, most of Mahmud's attacks were directed towards the temple towns of north India. A temple at
Somnath was among the most famous.

Security and stability replaced lawlessness and disorder.
ground_truth: Razia Sultan's nobles did not like being ruled by a woman. Some provincial governors revolted against her; she was defeated and imprisoned. She married her captor Altunia and tried to recover her throne, but both she and Altunia were killed in 1240 CE.
